name: Ahinadab
overview: Ahinadab was a male figure who served as one of King Solomon's twelve deputies, overseeing the district of Mahanaim. His role was part of the administrative organization established by Solomon to govern the kingdom effectively. Beyond his official capacity, Scripture does not provide additional personal details such as tribal affiliation or other notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahinadab means '[my] brother is willing,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name. This meaning highlights a willing or supportive character, though the name was not given directly by God. The biblical record mentions only this one name for him.
familyAndRelationships: Ahinadab is identified as the son of Iddo, establishing a clear father-son relationship in Scripture. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Ahinadab's significance lies in his administrative role under Solomon's reign, illustrating the organized governance that contributed to the kingdom's stability and prosperity. As one of the twelve deputies, he was entrusted with overseeing a key region, Mahanaim, demonstrating Solomon's delegation of authority to trusted leaders. His mention in the biblical record underscores the importance of faithful service in the leadership structure God allowed in Israel during Solomon's time.
